prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the active incretin peptide that enabled a new class of therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us ranked B035 first, but unanimity is not the argument. The case is a complete discovery chain: proglucagon processing, the identification of the truncated active GLP-1 peptide, its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions, and the receptor biology, followed by therapies with large randomized evidence in glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism has been confirmed independently for decades, so this is neither premature nor a drug-development story without a mechanistic foundation. A three-person prize built on Holst (physiology), Drucker (receptor biology and translational work) and Mojsov (the active peptide) keeps the emphasis on discovery, which is where this committee should place it.
statement.case_against: Credit is the weak point. Mojsov's priority on the active GLP-1(7-36) form is debated, Habener and other early proglucagon workers fall outside the credited list, and Knudsen, whose industrial work produced liraglutide and semaglutide, is excluded by the three-person limit. A prize that omits the developers of the drugs that actually reached patients could be read as honouring the physiology while leaving out the medicine. Long-term safety and durability of obesity treatment are also still accruing, although these do not touch the core discovery.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks B035 first with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and leaves Knudsen out as an industrial developer. He ranks BCR-ABL inhibition (B012) third, with the caveat that the earlier Philadelphia chromosome and oncogene discoveries are not credited.
responses.response: I agree on excluding Knudsen, though I hold the view with less confidence than he does, because the drug-development contribution is real and I would want the citation to acknowledge the therapeutic consequence. On B012 I share his reservation about the Rowley, Nowell and Witte groundwork. The imatinib story is mature and compelling, but its credited trio is mainly translational and industrial, which makes it a weaker physiology-or-medicine discovery than B035 and, in my view, weaker than B029 or B002 on conceptual originality.

responses.point: Sandberg places the unfolded protein response (Mori and Walter) second and cGAS-STING (B050) fourth, and calls cGAS-STING mechanistically strong but possibly early because therapeutic validation is lacking.
responses.response: I agree that cGAS-STING is early. Mechanism is solid, but STING agonists and inhibitors have not shown clinical benefit, and the autoimmune links are still largely associative. The unfolded protein response is not on our shortlist, so I will not argue it here. Among shortlisted candidates, B029 has the stronger combination of immunological novelty and confirmed patient benefit, so I would not put a mechanism with unproven translation ahead of it.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks optogenetics (B046) second and says that six credited people, three slots and a tool rather than a disease mechanism make the allocation a judgement call.
responses.response: I take the allocation problem seriously. The Nagel and Hegemann channelrhodopsin discovery is separable from the neuronal implementation by Deisseroth and Boyden, and Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims, so any trio is arbitrary to some degree. That is a stronger objection to B046 than to B035. I would also be cautious about a second tool-defining prize while clinical translation is still early. I do not rank it above B029 for that reason, though I would defer to the neuroscientists on the priority history.

responses.point: El Manira ranks B029 third and proposes only June and Sadelain, treating Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work as partly adjacent. He also flags that Eshhar's original CAR concept is not in the credited list.
responses.response: I think he is right that Rosenberg is the most debatable name, and I partly agree with narrowing to June and Sadelain. I would still not drop him lightly. Adoptive transfer of gene-engineered T cells, including the early clinical work, belongs to the same lineage. The omission of Eshhar is a more serious attribution problem that we cannot resolve from the supplied credit, and it is the main reason I place B029 as an alternative to B035 rather than alongside it.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's claim on the active GLP-1 peptide, relative to Habener and others, is strong enough for a place among three.
Whether the committee will frame the award as physiology and discovery or as drug development, which decides whether Knudsen should displace one of the three.
How to credit the original CAR concept (Eshhar) if B029 becomes the alternative.
Whether B002 is read as a fundamental discovery or as clinical development, and whether TNF discovery itself (Cerami, Old, Beutler) would need to be recognised.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B035. B002 (TNF blockade in rheumatoid arthritis) lies in my own field of rheumatology. This is a disciplinary proximity, not a documented personal or institutional tie to Feldmann or Maini, but I disclose it so the committee can weigh my views on that candidate accordingly.
